name: Emface

lead: Emface combines radiofrequency heating of the skin with electrical stimulation of facial muscles. It is used for smoother wrinkles, firmer muscle tone and a lifted look without needles.

RF energy heats the dermis to stimulate collagen remodelling, while stimulation makes the facial muscles contract. Headline figures such as 37% wrinkle improvement come from manufacturer-linked data; no independent peer-reviewed trial was found.

paras: It is typically a course of four sessions of about 20 minutes each in a clinic, with no needles or downtime.
No Emface-specific safety data were found. A 2025 study of non-surgical aesthetic treatments generally reports that complications are underreported.

web.title: Synchronized RF and HIFES in Asians (Lasers Surg Med)

chain: RF heats skin, stimulates facial muscles
angle.text: It is used as a needle-free way to smooth wrinkles and lift the face over a short course of sessions. RF heat builds collagen while muscle stimulation firms tone, giving a lifted, smoother face. The headline improvement figures come mainly from manufacturer-supported data.

lead: Emface is a facial treatment from BTL Aesthetics that delivers radiofrequency (RF) energy and high-intensity facial electrical stimulation (HIFES) through pads placed on the face. People have it done to smooth wrinkles, firm sagging skin and lift the cheeks, brows and jawline without needles, surgery or downtime.[1][2] It was launched in 2022 as the facial counterpart to BTL's Emsculpt body treatments.[2]

The RF component heats collagen and elastin fibres in the skin to prompt remodelling, while HIFES contracts facial muscles thousands of times per session to improve tone, so one treatment addresses both skin quality and the muscle layer beneath it.[1][2] The recommended course is four 20-minute sessions, and BTL reports best results 6 to 12 weeks after the final one.[2] A separate submental applicator targets the area under the chin.[1]

BTL reports averages of 37 percent wrinkle reduction, 30 percent more facial muscle tone and 23 percent lifting across nine studies.[2] A 2025 pre-post study in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine of 15 adults found improved forehead lift, firmness and crow's feet, with no serious adverse events.[3]
infobox: Described as FDA-cleared for facial wrinkles [1]

paras: The RF component heats the dermis to stimulate collagen remodelling, while HIFES induces contractions in facial muscles, particularly in the cheeks.[1] It is applied to the cheeks, jawline, eyebrows and forehead, and a separate submental applicator targets the area under the chin.[1] The device is described as FDA-cleared for facial wrinkles.[1]

Practical Dermatology reports the recommended protocol as four 20-minute sessions spaced 2 to 14 days apart, with no pre- or post-treatment preparation and no downtime.[2] Grokipedia gives a spacing of 5 to 10 days.[1] In the 2025 Thailand study, treatment used electrode pads on the forehead and both cheeks, once weekly for four weeks.[3]

BTL's figures are averages of 37 percent wrinkle reduction, 30 percent facial muscle tone and 23 percent lifting, from nine clinical studies of people who completed the course.[2] For the submental applicator, Grokipedia repeats a 30.37 percent reduction in submental fat volume on MRI at three months.[1] These figures are manufacturer-linked.

The 2025 study reported no serious adverse events, and average pain scores fell from about 3.5 to about 1.6 out of 10 across sessions.[3] A broad 2025 mixed-methods analysis of non-surgical aesthetic treatments reports that complications in the category are underreported and inconsistently regulated, without being specific to Emface.[4]

A prospective, evaluator-blinded, pre-post study at Siriraj Hospital enrolled 15 adults aged 41 to 62 with mild to moderate skin laxity, treated with four weekly sessions of synchronized RF and HIFES. Forehead lift peaked at 1 month and remained statistically significant at 6 months, firmness improved by about 81 percent at 6 months, and crow's feet wrinkles improved by roughly 11 to 12 percent. Forehead and cheek wrinkles did not change significantly, and cheek lift at 6 months was not statistically significant. The study had no control group.[3]
A registered trial started in December 2025 combines Emface with another BTL device for temporomandibular joint pain, a medical use.[5]

timeline.event: US commercial launch as BTL's facial counterpart to Emsculpt.[1][2]
Lasers in Surgery and Medicine publishes a 15-person pre-post study of synchronized RF and HIFES.[3]
